analyst_view.overall: A relegation six-pointer: ADO Den Haag are 17th with 9 points and FC Utrecht 15th with 12 after 13 games, and Utrecht have conceded 37 goals, the second most in the league. Both clubs have changed coach this month: ADO sacked Robin Peter on 2 November and Maurice Steijn lost 3-0 at Ajax on his return last Sunday after Matteo Waem was sent off; Utrecht sacked Anthony Correia on 22 November after a 2-3 home loss to promoted Cambuur, and Jong Utrecht coach Mark Otten takes his first game as interim. Waem's ban is already in the numbers; ADO otherwise report almost a full squad (only striker Luka Reischl, who has not scored this season, is out with a groin injury), while Utrecht winger Angel Alarcon missed the Cambuur game with a slight injury and full-back Niklas Vesterlund pulled out at the last minute, both unclear for Sunday. Utrecht's director said stability and the goals conceded are the first job for Otten, and with so much at stake for both I lean a little lower on goals and a little higher on cards. News was thin four days out: no preview for this match was published yet, so the view rests on match reports, club news and the coaching changes.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, high because both defences leak (ADO 28 conceded, Utrecht 37), and they already add about +6% for Utrecht because ADO defender Waem is banned. I lean slightly lower: Utrecht's interim coach Mark Otten has been told stability and cutting the goals conceded come first, and a bottom-four meeting with two new coaches often starts cautious. That takes it to about 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners, with Utrecht taking a bit more (5.0) and recent form already counted (ADO slightly below expected for, Utrecht slightly above). Neither coaching change points clearly to more or less wide play yet: Steijn's only game was played with ten men at Ajax, and Otten has no Eredivisie match behind him. I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards, with Utrecht's busier recent card count (+3%) already in; no referee is named yet and the brief flags no stakes. This is a tense relegation six-pointer between two sides under new coaches, and ADO picked up a red card and a late heavy challenge (Sylla on Mokio) at Ajax, so I lean mildly higher, to about 3.7. If the referee is named, his record will be counted by the numbers, not by me.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.4 shots, and they already add about +15% to Utrecht for their recent shot volume against a side that has allowed many shots. Against Cambuur Utrecht had one shot on target before half-time and then pushed hard, which fits that count; Otten's focus on defending could trim it, but that is only a hunch, so I stay at about 31.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target (4.9 ADO, 5.8 Utrecht), with recent form already counted on both sides. ADO managed only four shots at Ajax, but with ten men for most of the game, so that says little about Sunday; Utrecht's striker Artem Stepanov scored against Cambuur and Alarcon's fitness is unclear. Nothing the numbers can't see points either way, so I stay at about 10.7.
